Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 0.23% to 25,045 but decliners led 1,533 to 1,026
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +2.03% weighted by turnover, against -0.45% for the median stock, a gap of 2.5 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

TRANSWORLD SHIPPING LINES LIMITED rose 20.0% on 176 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about quarterly results, “TRANSWORLD SHIPPING LINES LIMITED has submitted to the Exchange, the financial results for the period ended September 30, 2026.”.

Repco Home Finance Limited rose 11.9% on 93 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Link of Recording”.

Gujarat Natural Resources Limited rose 6.7% on 173 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Eurozone bond yields fall as lower energy prices ease inflation concerns”.

Aarti Drugs Limited rose 11.1% on 160 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Govt cannot eradicate drugs without public support: Amit Shah - The Statesman”.

What happened
Breaking
Fed officials open door to a quicker round of rate hikes as inflation worsens
Fed officials signaled faster interest rate hikes after US inflation surpassed projections. Tighter Fed policy widens the US-India yield differential, driving foreign institutional capital out of emerging markets and weakening the rupee. This trend compresses valuation multiples across high-beta growth stocks while providing temporary currency margin gains to IT exporters. Watch the upcoming US core PCE print for confirmation.
Reuters Business · +1 other
Wall St ends lower as hot inflation data, Fed comments heighten rate worries
Major US equity indices closed lower as hawkish Fed comments and persistent inflation triggered a sell-off in growth assets. This risk-off sentiment spills over to Indian equities through foreign fund outflows in liquid large-cap stocks like HDFC Bank and Reliance. Prolonged weakness in US markets increases the global cost of capital and depresses Indian market valuation multiples.
Reuters Business · +3 others
Fed's Logan calls for two more rate hikes, possibly rapidly
Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan advocated for two additional rate hikes to counter persistent service-sector inflation. Higher US terminal rates push up US Treasury yields, narrowing the spread with Indian sovereign bonds. This spread compression triggers foreign institutional outflows from Indian financial markets, raising domestic borrowing costs and putting rate-sensitive banking and real estate sectors under pressure.
Reuters Business · +2 others
Connected to your data
OMC stocks: Brent slips below $90 to hit over 2-month low amid Iran peace hopes; Will HPCL, BPCL and IOC benefit?
Brent crude fell below $90 per barrel to a three-month low as Middle East supply disruption fears subsided. Lower crude prices expand gross marketing margins for fuel retailers HPCL, BPCL, and IOC, while reducing raw material input costs for paint manufacturers and specialty chemical firms. The price drop also lowers India's oil import bill and eases current account pressures.
Mint Markets · +1 other
Eurozone bond yields fall as lower energy prices ease inflation concerns
Eurozone government bond yields fell, with Germany's 10-year yield dropping to 3.25% as regional energy prices declined. Lower energy inflation reduces economic contraction risks across Europe, stabilizing end-user demand. This macro relief helps sustain order books and revenue realizations for Indian IT exporters, auto component suppliers, and textile companies with high revenue exposure to European markets.

Your themes
Microsoft tops Nvidia's market cap for first time since June 2025
Microsoft surpassed Nvidia in market capitalization as hardware valuations cooled while enterprise software demand stabilized. This shift reflects a rotation from hardware capex toward software monetization, offering valuation support for Indian IT majors like TCS and Infosys if US enterprise tech budgets shift toward application deployment.

Wall St slips as hot inflation data fuels rate-hike jitters; Nvidia down 4%
Higher than expected US inflation data sparked concerns of further Federal Reserve rate hikes, while Brent crude dropped below $90 a barrel. Higher US yields threaten foreign portfolio outflows and rupee weakness, but lower crude prices reduce input costs for Indian paint, auto, and specialty chemical companies. Friday's US retail sales data will confirm persistent demand pressure.

Wells Fargo upgrades US AI infrastructure view after chip selloff
Wells Fargo upgraded its US AI infrastructure outlook, citing sustained hyper-scaler capital expenditure after a sharp selloff in semiconductor shares. High cloud capex supports order books for Indian engineering services firms and electronics manufacturers linked to global data center construction. Quarterly capex guidance from Alphabet and Amazon will confirm execution timelines.

Tesla, SpaceX CEO Musk praises former friend Google co-founder Larry Page’s vision for future of computing: Here’s why
Elon Musk's comments on shifting global computing capacity into space are speculative long-term vision statements with no near-term material impact on Indian equities.

Cabinet nod for Rs 31,387-cr AI data centre in Vizag district - The Hans India
The Andhra Pradesh cabinet approved a ₹31,387 crore AI data center project in Visakhapatnam. This domestic capacity expansion drives direct order inflows for capital goods, industrial power, and cooling equipment vendors like Larsen & Toubro, Cummins India, and Schneider Electric Infrastructure. Land allotment timelines over the next quarter will confirm the execution schedule.

The turn of the tide: Foreign investors return, signalling longer India bet
Foreign portfolio investors bought ₹53,172 crore of equities in early November, ending a ten-month streak of net monthly outflows. Rebounding foreign flows provide immediate liquidity support to large-cap financial and consumption stocks while supporting the rupee. Fortnightly NSDL balance sheet disclosures will confirm whether these institutional allocations remain sustained.

Anthropic's path from AI startup to industry-defining IPO
Anthropic's prospective US listing has no direct transmission mechanism to Indian equities.

Drone attack leaves part of Ukraine's Kryvyi Rih without power
This localized Ukrainian power disruption has no direct transmission mechanism to global commodity prices or Indian equities.
Reuters Business
Blackstone to buy about 16% of IIFL Finance in latest foreign bet on Indian lenders
Blackstone acquired a 16% stake in IIFL Finance, providing direct primary capital to the non-banking financial company. The foreign investment strengthens Tier-1 capital adequacy and restores market confidence following recent regulatory restrictions on its gold loan portfolio. Track IIFL Finance's borrowing spreads in corporate bond markets to confirm whether capital backing reduces its funding costs.
Reuters Business
Macro and economy
VIEW Hot October inflation report rattles markets
US headline consumer inflation rose 0.4% sequentially in October, pushing Treasury yields higher as market expectations for monetary easing receded. Rising US yields strengthen the dollar and narrow rate differentials, driving foreign institutional capital outflows from emerging market equities and weighing on the rupee. Net daily foreign institutional investor sales figures will confirm the scale of capital flight.
Reuters Business · +1 other
US consumer prices rise above expectations in October
US core consumer prices rose above expectations in October, driven by sticky services inflation. Elevated US interest rates prolong tight liquidity for Indian corporates issuing offshore dollar debt and limit the Reserve Bank of India's headroom to cut repo rates. Federal funds futures pricing for the December policy meeting will confirm rate path expectations.
ET Markets · +1 other
Higher input costs drag MRF Q2 net profit down 23%
MRF reported a 22.8% year-on-year drop in second-quarter net profit despite revenue rising 17.4% to Rs 8,660.19 crore. Spiking natural rubber and crude-linked raw material expenses squeezed gross operating margins, highlighting sector-wide cost inflation for tyre makers such as CEAT and Apollo Tyres. Domestic RSS-4 grade rubber spot prices will confirm if margin contraction persists into the third quarter.
ET Markets
Wall Street regulator poised to bring charges against Kalshi, Politico reports
This US regulatory enforcement action against a domestic prediction contracts platform has no transmission mechanism to Indian listed equities.
Reuters Business
Companies and earnings
US midterm results may ease India's oil import bill, but tariff risks stay - Business Standard
Expected US policy shifts toward expanded oil and gas leasing could ease Brent crude prices toward 70 dollars per barrel. For India, lower energy costs reduce import bills, protect gross margins for chemical and paint manufacturers, and support the rupee. Universal US tariff threats remain the primary risk, which would compress export realisations for domestic pharmaceutical and IT services companies.
Geopolitics
Blackstone to invest ₹5,000 crore in IIFL Finance for 16% stake
Blackstone is infusing 5,000 crore rupees into IIFL Finance for a 16 percent fully diluted stake, anchoring a larger 6,414 crore rupee capital raise. The transaction bolsters the lender's Tier-1 capital ratio, reducing wholesale funding costs after recent regulatory restrictions on its gold loan book. Peer non-bank financial companies like Manappuram Finance will see equity valuations tied increasingly to institutional backing and funding security.
livemint.com · +1 other
Global Renewable Energy Capacity Set To Grow By 4,800 GW By 2031, With Solar Leading Expansion—IEA - SolarQuarter
The International Energy Agency projects 4,800 gigawatts of global renewable capacity additions by 2031, led predominantly by solar installations. This massive rollout secures multi-year order backlogs and export demand for Indian module manufacturers, including Waaree Energies and Premier Energies. Domestic engineering and construction firms like Sterling and Wilson should benefit as developers accelerate execution before domestic module import tariffs increase.
Order wins and capex
Chipmakers warn AI demand is creating bottlenecks in automotive supply chain
Semiconductor foundries are shifting production capacity toward high-margin artificial intelligence processors, causing renewed delivery bottlenecks for mature-node automotive chips. Protracted component lead times threaten assembly schedules and inflate working capital requirements for automakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra. Tier-1 auto component suppliers, including Bosch and Uno Minda, face higher spot-procurement costs that will compress their gross margins over coming quarters.
ET Markets
Geopolitics
China curbs expose India's solar, battery machinery dependence; manufacturers scout for alternatives - Moneycontrol.com
China has placed export restrictions on advanced manufacturing equipment for solar wafer, cell, and battery production, forcing Indian producers to scout for costlier European or domestic alternatives. This raises capital expenditure intensity and risks commissioning delays for cell manufacturers including Waaree Energies, Premier Energies, and Tata Power under the production-linked incentive scheme. Project execution timelines in upcoming quarterly investor presentations will show the extent of plant delays.
Solar and green energy
Fed’s Bowman Warns of Stock Correction If AI Bets Don’t Pan Out
Federal Reserve Governor Michelle Bowman warned that stretched US equity valuations risk a sharp sell-off if corporate earnings from artificial intelligence investments fall short of high capital outlays. Any tech de-rating in New York triggers foreign portfolio outflows from India via emerging market exchange-traded funds. It also directly threatens order-book momentum and billing rates for Tier-1 Indian IT exporters reliant on discretionary US enterprise software spending.
